metrics.label: MTTR
metrics.basis: median of 51 incidents in the last 15 days
metrics.meaning: Median time from failure starting to service being restored — detect, acknowledge and mitigate combined.

metrics.label: MTTA
metrics.basis: median across incidents a human handled; auto-remediated ones excluded
metrics.meaning: Median time from an alert firing to a human taking ownership of it.

metrics.label: MTTD
metrics.meaning: Median time between a failure beginning and monitoring noticing it.

metrics.label: MTBF
metrics.meaning: Mean hours between incidents. Rising is good — failures are getting rarer.

metrics.label: Availability
metrics.meaning: Mean availability across all monitored services for the window.

metrics.label: Worst budget burn
metrics.meaning: Fraction of the period's error budget already spent by the worst service. Above 1 means the SLO is already missed.

metrics.label: Alert noise
metrics.meaning: Share of alerts that closed with no incident and no action. This is what burns out on-call.

metrics.label: Alerts per incident
metrics.meaning: How many alerts fire for each real incident. High values mean grouping rules are not doing their job.

metrics.label: Auto-remediated
metrics.meaning: Incidents automation closed without waking anyone. The single best lever on on-call load.

metrics.label: Escalation rate
metrics.meaning: Incidents the first responder could not resolve alone. A proxy for runbook and access gaps.

metrics.label: RCA coverage
metrics.meaning: Share of critical and major incidents that have a written root cause.

metrics.label: Repeat incidents
metrics.meaning: Incidents with the same service and root cause as an earlier one. Repeats mean the fix did not stick.

metrics.label: Ack SLA met
metrics.meaning: Incidents acknowledged inside the promise for their severity — 5 minutes for a SEV1.

metrics.label: Open incidents
metrics.meaning: Incidents not yet fully resolved, at any stage of the pipeline.

pipeline.detail: Signals that crossed a rule threshold.
Alerts left once duplicates were grouped and known-noise was suppressed.
Alert groups a human or policy promoted to a declared incident.
Incidents someone has taken ownership of.
Customer impact has ended, whether or not the cause is understood.
Incidents with a written, agreed root cause.
Written up and shared, with actions assigned.
